headline: Google uses your media for AI training by default; here's how to opt out
summary: A recent, under-the-radar update to Google's privacy settings now uses your uploaded images, audio, and video from services like Search, Maps, and Translate to train its AI models unless you manually opt out.
details: A recent Google privacy setting change now allows the company to store your media, including images, files, audio, and video recordings, to improve its AI models. This means media uploaded to Google Search services is used for AI training unless you specifically opt out.

The update, announced in June via customer email, expanded AI training data collection. It essentially opted people into this expanded training under the guise of offering more control over saved history and personalized recommendations.

This applies to services beyond Google Search, such as Maps, Shopping, Flights, Hotels, Translate, and News. For example, images from Google Lens or audio from voice input in the Google app or Translate practice can now be saved for AI training.

Google directly confirms this media-training use, stating that "your saved media is also used to develop and improve Google services and technologies, including AI models and safety measures." Its help documentation notes this history is used to train generative AI models and for safety with human reviewers.

Users can regain control by changing preferences on the Search Services History page. Here, you can uncheck the "Save Media" box separately or configure automatic data deletion after 3, 18, or 36 months.

The update also separated "Web & App Activity" from a new "Search data" setting, which is on by default. This means previous opt-outs for Web & App Activity no longer impact Google Search services, as it is now a distinct option.
